title: Fantasy Player News
description: Breaking Fantasy Football player news along with the impact for fantasy managers

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Case Keenum quiet in relief in Week 5
items.desc: Case Keenum completed 11-of-19 pass attempts for 108 yards and one interception while also rushing once for four yards in the Bears' 31-7 loss to the Green Bay Packers in Week 5.
items.impact: Keenum was called on late in the Week 5 contest with Tyson Bagent struggling behind center, but was unable to get the Chicago offense back on track in the loss. The veteran could be relegated back to a No. 2/No .3 role with Caleb Williams (hamstring) close to returning for head coach Ben Johnson ahead of a Week 6 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Tyson Bagent struggles behind center prior to benching in Week 5
items.desc: Tyson Bagent completed 12-of-21 pass attempts for 87 yards and two interceptions while also rushing three times for 17 yards and one fumble lost in the Bears' 31-7 loss to the Green Bay Packers in Week 5.
items.impact: Bagent would be relegated to the bench late in the contest, finishing under 100 passing yards in two of three contests. The quarterback could return to a backup role if No. 1 signal caller Caleb Williams (hamstring) is able to return for a Week 6 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: D'Andre Swift reaches end zone in Week 5 loss to Packers
items.desc: D'Andre Swift carried the ball nine times for 43 yards and one touchdown while also catching four of his five targets for 30 yards in the Bears' 31-7 Week 5 loss to the Green Bay Packers.
items.impact: Swift continues a strong start to the season out of the Chicago backfield, finishing with over 70 offensive yards in each of the first five games. The running back remains a reliable option out of the backfield in all formats, with a Week 6 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons up next.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Luther Burden III leads underwhelming passing offense in Week 5 loss
items.desc: Luther Burden III hauled in four of his six targets for a team-leading 47 yards while also rushing four times for two yards in the Bears' 31-7 Week 5 loss to the Green Bay Packers.
items.impact: Burden III has seen consistent involvement in the Chicago passing attack to begin the season, recording four or more receptions in four of five contests. The wideout remains one of the more stable pass-catching options for head coach Ben Johnson ahead of a Week 6 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Rome Odunze sees nine targets in Week 5 loss
items.desc: Rome Odunze hauled in three of his team-leading nine targets for 40 yards with a fumble lost in the Bears' 31-7 Week 5 loss to the Green Bay Packers.
items.impact: Odunze has struggled to make a consistent impact in the Chicago passing attack, finishing with less than 60 receiving yards in four of five contests. The wideout remains a risky pass-catching option in all formats ahead of a Week 6 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Colston Loveland quiet in Week 5 loss
items.desc: Colston Loveland caught two of his five targets for 19 yards in the Bears' 31-7 loss to the Green Bay Packers in Week 5.
items.impact: Loveland has seen inconsistent involvement in the Chicago passing attack to begin the season, recording two receptions or less in three of the first five contests. The tight end remains difficult to trust in all formats ahead of a Week 6 contest against the Atlanta Falcons.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Kalif Raymond bottled up in Week 5 loss
items.desc: Kalif Raymond hauled in three of his four targets for six yards while also rushing once for a loss of two yards in the Bears' 31-7 Week 5 loss to the Green Bay Packers.
items.impact: Raymond has fallen back to earth after a strong start to the season, finishing with less than 10 receiving yards in each of the last two contests. The speedy wideout will look to get back to offering head coach Ben Johnson another impactful pass-catcher ahead of a Week 6 contest against the Atlanta Falcons.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Roschon Johnson sees 10 touches in Week 5 loss
items.desc: Roschon Johnson rushed five times for six yards while also catching five of his seven targets for 34 yards in the Bears' 31-7 loss to the Green Bay Packers in Week 5.
items.impact: Johnson has seen increased involvement out of the Chicago backfield of late, recording five or more touches in each of the last two games. The running back remains difficult to trust when the Chicago backfield is fully healthy, with a Week 6 contest against the Atlanta Falcons up next.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Cole Kmet quiet in Week 5
items.desc: Cole Kmet caught one of his two targets for eight yards in the Bears' 31-7 loss to the Green Bay Packers in Week 5.
items.impact: Kmet has seen minimal involvement in the Chicago offense to this point, finishing with two receptions or less in each of the first five contests. The tight end remains one of many risky-pass catching options ahead of a Week 6 contest against the Atlanta Falcons.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Zavion Thomas sees two touches in Week 5
items.desc: Zavion Thomas caught his only target for 11 yards while also rushing once for 11 yards in the Bears' 31-7 loss to the Green Bay Packers in Week 5.
items.impact: Thomas has been non-existent in the Chicago offense to begin the season, seeing one target or less in each of the first five contests. The wideout can be left off rosters in all formats ahead of a Week 6 contest against the Atlanta Falcons.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Jahdae Walker sees one target in Week 5
items.desc: Jahdae Walker failed to catch his only target in the Bears' 31-7 loss to the Green Bay Packers in Week 5.
items.impact: Walker has been an afterthought in the Chicago passing attack early on, seeing one target or less in each of the first five contests. The wideout remains best left off rosters in all formats ahead of a Week 6 contest against the Atlanta Falcons.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Jordan Love tosses two touchdowns in Week 5 win over Bears
items.desc: Jordan Love completed 25-of-31 pass attempts for 367 yards and two touchdowns while also rushing once for six yards in the Packers' 31-7 Week 5 win over the Chicago Bears.
items.impact: Love has flashed impactful output behind center, passing for over 300 yards in three of the first five contests. The quarterback will look to take advantage of a generous Dallas Cowboys defense in Week 6.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Christian Watson hauls in two touchdowns in Week 5 win over Bears
items.desc: Christian Watson hauled in six of his team-leading eight targets for a team-high 143 yards and two touchdowns in the Packers' 31-7 Week 5 win over the Chicago Bears.
items.impact: Watson has had a nose for the end zone to begin the season, hauling in one or more touchdowns in four of the first five games. The wideout remains a dynamic pass-catching option in a Green Bay passing attack looking for more consistent output, with a Week 6 contest against the Dallas Cowboys up next.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Matthew Golden surpasses 100 yards in Week 5 win
items.desc: Matthew Golden hauled in six of his seven targets for 123 yards in the Packers' 31-7 Week 5 win over the Chicago Bears.
items.impact: Golden has seen steady involvement in the Green Bay passing attack to begin the season, recording over 90 receiving yards in three of the first five games. The wideout remains one of the more impactful pass-catching options for quarterback Jordan Love, with a Week 6 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys up next.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Tucker Kraft sees six touches in Week 5
items.desc: Tucker Kraft caught all five of his targets for 64 yards while also rushing once for two yards in the Packers' 31-7 win over the Chicago Bears in Week 5.
items.impact: Kraft has seen increased involvement in the Green Bay passing attack of late, logging five or more targets in each of his last three contests. The tight end will look to offer more impactful output moving forward, with a Week 6 contest against the Dallas Cowboys up next.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: MarShawn Lloyd rushes for two touchdowns in Week 5 win
items.desc: MarShawn Lloyd carried the ball 10 times for 31 yards and two touchdowns while also catching one of his two targets for six yards in the Packers' 31-7 Week 5 win over the Chicago Bears.
items.impact: Lloyd has made minimal impact as the primary option in the Green Bay backfield to begin the season, rushing for less than 40 yards in each of the first five games. The running back remains difficult to trust despite his No. 1 role ahead of a Week 6 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Kaleb Johnson quiet in Week 5
items.desc: Kaleb Johnson rushed seven times for 26 yards in the Packers' 31-7 win over the Chicago Bears in Week 5.
items.impact: Johnson has struggled to make an impact out of the Green Bay backfield to this point, finishing with less than 45 rushing yards in each of his four contests. The running back remains difficult to trust ahead of a Week 6 contest against the Dallas Cowboys.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Pierre Strong Jr. sees eight touches in Week 5
items.desc: Pierre Strong Jr. rushed five times for seven yards while also catching three of his four targets for 11 yards in the Packers' 31-7 win over the Chicago Bears in Week 5.
items.impact: Strong Jr. struggled to make an impact in his first game action of the season, averaging just 1.4 yards per carry in a winning effort. The running back can remain off rosters in all formats ahead of a Week 6 contest against the Dallas Cowboys.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Bo Melton catches three passes in Week 5
items.desc: Bo Melton caught three of his four targets for 20 yards in the Packers' 31-7 win over the Chicago Bears in Week 5.
items.impact: Melton has been minimally involved in the Green Bay passing attack to this point, finishing with less than two targets in four of the first five games. The wideout can be left off rosters in all formats ahead of a Week 6 contest against the Dallas Cowboys.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Skyy Moore sees one target prior to exiting in Week 5
items.desc: Skyy Moore failed to catch his only target before exiting in the Packers' 31-7 win over the Chicago Bears in Week 5.
items.impact: Moore remains minimally involved in the Green Bay passing attack, recording two receptions or less in four of five contests. The wideout can remain off rosters in all formats ahead of a Week 6 contest against the Dallas Cowboys.

items.author: Matthew Adam
items.title: Isaiah Davis sees three touches in Week 5
items.desc: Isaiah Davis carried the ball twice for eight yards and caught one of his two targets for a nine-yard gain in a 17-12 win over the Browns in Week 5.
items.impact: While it wasn't a big game, it was a step in the right direction for Davis as he didn't receive a touch in Week 4. He will continue to back up Braelon Allen moving forward, at least until Breece Hall (quad) is ready to return. The Jets will face the Patriots in Week 6.

items.author: Matthew Adam
items.title: Braelon Allen finds the end zone in Week 5
items.desc: Braelon Allen carried the ball 24 times for 116 yards and a touchdown while catching one of his four targets for no gain in a 17-12 win over the Browns in Week 5.
items.impact: Allen looked excellent on a rainy afternoon at MetLife Stadium. He ripped off an impressive 22-yard touchdown run to put the Jets up for good in the fourth quarter. Allen will be on the RB2 radar in Week 6 against the Patriots.

items.author: Matthew Adam
items.title: Geno Smith throws TD in Week 5 win
items.desc: Geno Smith completed 17 of his 30 passes for 182 yards and one touchdown while adding seven yards on five carries in a 17-12 win over the Browns in Week 5.
items.impact: Smith struggled in rainy conditions at home in MetLife Stadium but he was still able to lead his team to the win. He lost a fumble on a strip-sack in the fourth quarter while his lone touchdown pass went to Garrett Wilson on a 32-yard connection in the first quarter. Smith has now thrown for six touchdowns and zero interceptions through five games. He will be on the QB2 radar in Week 6's road matchup against the Patriots.

items.author: Matthew Adam
items.title: Browns D/ST notches four sacks in Week 5
items.desc: The Browns D/ST allowed 17 points while picking up four sacks and forcing two turnovers in a 17-12 loss to the Jets in Week 5.
items.impact: Cleveland's defense played well on a rainy afternoon at MetLife Stadium. They got a strip-sack on Geno Smith in the fourth quarter while also recovering a Kenyon Sadiq fumble. The Browns will now take on the Ravens at home in Week 6.

items.author: Matthew Adam
items.title: Andre Szmyt hits two FGs in Week 5
items.desc: Andre Szmyt hit both of his field-goal tries while missing his lone extra point in a 17-12 loss to the Jets in Week 5.
items.impact: Szmyt hit field goals from 25 and 41 yards out. His lone extra-point try went off the right goalpost on a rainy day at MetLife Stadium. Szmyt has now connected on all 10 of his field goals this season. He will head back home to Cleveland to face off against the Ravens in Week 6.

items.author: Matthew Adam
items.title: Harold Fannin Jr. held to one catch in Week 5
items.desc: Harold Fannin Jr. caught one of his four targets for four yards in a 17-12 loss to the Jets in Week 5.
items.impact: It was the first time in Fannin's 21-game NFL career that he was held to fewer than two catches, although a rainy afternoon at MetLife Stadium may have played into the slow outing. The second-year tight end now has 18 catches for 157 yards and three touchdowns through five games. He will look to bounce back at home in Week 6 against the Ravens.

items.author: Matthew Adam
items.title: Isaiah Bond leads Browns in receiving in Week 5
items.desc: Isaiah Bond caught three of his seven targets for 74 yards in a 17-12 loss to the Jets in Week 5.
items.impact: Bond led the Browns in receiving yards while tying for the lead with his seven targets. He saw additional opportunities with KC Concepcion leaving during the game with a concussion. If Concepcion is unable to clear the league's concussion protocol, Bond would be in play as a flex option in deeper leagues against the Ravens in Week 6.

items.author: Matthew Adam
items.title: Jerry Jeudy catches three passes in Week 5
items.desc: Jerry Jeudy caught three of his seven targets for 19 yards in a 17-12 loss to the Jets in Week 5.
items.impact: Jeudy tied for the lead with seven targets, but he wasn't able to do much with the opportunities. The veteran wideout has been quiet through the first five games of the season, catching just eight passes for 81 yards. He will not be a recommended fantasy option in Week 6 against Baltimore

items.author: Matthew Adam
items.title: Denzel Boston finds the end zone in Week 5 loss
items.desc: Denzel Boston caught three of his seven targets for 46 yards and a touchdown in a 17-12 loss to the Jets in Week 5.
items.impact: Boston's impressive rookie season continues. The emerging star pass-catcher hauled in a 29-yard touchdown from Deshaun Watson in the fourth quarter, giving the Browns a temporary lead. Boston has now caught three touchdowns through five games. He will be on the WR3 radar in Week 6's home game against the Ravens.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Marvin Harrison Jr. headed to Houston
items.desc: Marvin Harrison Jr. has been traded to the Houston Texans, per a report that came out after the Texans win over the Titans.
items.impact: Harrison had worn out his welcome in Arizona, and will now be reunited with his college QB. He will look to rebuild his value with his new team, and hopefully provide a viable No.2 target behind Nico Collins. As for the likes of Jaylin Noel, Xavier Hutchinson, Tank Dell, and the injured Jayden Higgins, this will certainly cap their ceilings.

items.author: Matthew Adam
items.title: Raheim Sanders runs for 12 yards in Week 5
items.desc: Raheim Sanders carried the ball three times for 12 yards while catching his lone target for a one-yard gain in a 17-12 loss to the Jets in Week 5.
items.impact: Sanders continues to see a handful of touches for the Browns behind Quinshon Judkins. The veteran will now prepare to take on the Ravens at home in Week 6.

items.author: Matthew Adam
items.title: Quinshon Judkins runs for 44 yards in Week 5 loss
items.desc: Quinshon Judkins carried the ball 14 times for 44 yards while catching three of his four targets for six yards in a 17-12 loss to the Jets in Week 5.
items.impact: It was a rainy day at MetLife Stadium, but Judkins was unable to get much going on the ground in the close loss. The second-year running back now has run for 221 yards and one touchdown through five games. He will be an RB3 in fantasy heading into Week 6's home game against the Ravens.

items.author: Matthew Adam
items.title: Deshaun Watson struggles in Week 5
items.desc: Deshaun Watson completed 15 of his 33 passes for 155 yards and one touchdown while adding six rushes for 40 yards in a 17-12 loss to the Jets in Week 5.
items.impact: Watson fumbled four times, losing one, while taking eight sacks. It was a rainy day  at MetLife Stadium, which explains some of Watson's troubles, but he still needed to play better. His lone touchdown pass was a 29-yard strike to Denzel Boston in the fourth quarter. The owner of seven touchdown passes and two interceptions through five games, Watson will look to bounce back at home against the Ravens in Week 6.

items.author: Jesse Garcia
items.title: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) ruled out
items.desc: The Patriots have ruled out RB TreVeyon Henderson for the remainder of Week 5 with an ankle injury.
items.impact: Henderson was injured in the first half and will not returning, leaving Rhamondre Stevenson as the primary running back. Henderson will finish the day with 22 rushing yards on four carries and one reception for 16 yards.

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: Eagles D/ST allows just 19 points to high-powered Jaguars
items.desc: The Eagles defense surrendered only 19 points on 408 yards of total offense, coming up with two sacks and one interception in Sunday's 19-17 loss.
items.impact: The Eagles played a bend-don't-break brand of defense Sunday, and it was almost enough to get them an upset victory over the Jaguars. The unit really clamped down in the red zone and held the Jacksonville running backs to just 3.2 yards per carry on the day. The Eagles will face another stiff test against the Panthers in Week 6.

items.author: Jesse Garcia
items.title: George Holani (ribs) officially active for Week 5
items.desc: Seahawks RB George Holani (ribs) is officially active for a Week 5 matchup with the 49ers.
items.impact: Holani was considered questionable to play Sunday. He will serve as the primary backup to Emanuel Wilson against the 49ers.

items.author: Jesse Garcia
items.title: George Kittle (illness) officially active for Week 5
items.desc: 49ers TE George Kittle (illness) is officially active for a Week 5 matchup with the Seahawks.
items.impact: It was announced that Kittle was dealing with an illness, but the star tight end will suit up and play Sunday. Kittle should slot in as a TE1 this week despite the illness.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Ladd McConkey (foot) active for Week 5
items.desc: Ladd McConkey (foot) is officially active for Week 5 for the Los Angeles Chargers against the Denver Broncos Sunday.
items.impact: McConkey was originally not expected to suit up, but is good to go after testing the injured foot ahead of Sunday's contest. The wideout will look to offer head coach Jim Harbaugh an impactful pass-catching option as part of a banged up Chargers offense, but could be limited against the Broncos Sunday.

items.author: Jesse Garcia
items.title: Ben Skowronek (calf) ruled out
items.desc: The Steelers have ruled out WR Ben Skowronek (calf) for the remainder of the game with the Colts.
items.impact: Skowronek and Roman Wilson will not return for the Steelers in the second half. He did not receive a target prior to his injury.

items.author: Jesse Garcia
items.title: Roman Wilson (finger) ruled out
items.desc: The Steelers have ruled out WR Roman Wilson for the remainder of the game against the Colts with a finger injury.
items.impact: Wilson will finish without a catch on one target Sunday. With Wilson out, Germie Bernard and DK Metcalf will serve as the two top pass catchers for Aaron Rodgers for the remainder of the game.

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: Jalen Hurts tosses one touchdown in Sunday's loss
items.desc: Jalen Hurts completed 21 of 40 passes for 220 yards with one touchdown and no interceptions in Sunday's 19-17 loss to the Jaguars.
items.impact: Given the injuries in the Eagles' backfield, it was certainly surprising that Hurts only carried the ball twice for two yards in Week 5. He did make some plays with his arm, but the passing attack was inefficient overall. Hurts led what looked like a certain game-winning drive late in the fourth quarter, as the Eagles grabbed a 17-16 lead on a 48-yard FG with eight seconds remaining. However, the Jaguars were able to steal the game back with some clutch special-teams play. Hurts still has his work cut out for him in the short term, with top WR DeVonta Smith (hamstring) still trying to make it back and several new faces on the offensive line. The Panthers await in Week 6.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Riley Moss (ribs) inactive for Week 5
items.desc: Riley Moss (ribs) is inactive for Week 5 for the Denver Broncos against the Los Angeles Chargers.
items.impact: Moss was unable to progress throughout the practice week for head coach Sean Payton, joining fellow starting cornerback Pat Surtain II (ankle) out the lineup against the Chargers Sunday.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Pat Surtain II (ankle) inactive for Week 5
items.desc: Pat Surtain II (ankle) is inactive for Week 5 for the Denver Broncos against the Los Angeles Chargers.
items.impact: Surtain II joins Riley Moss out of the Denver secondary for head coach Sean Payton, leaving the Broncos defense without one of its top playmakers against the winless Chargers Sunday.

items.author: Jesse Garcia
items.title: David Montgomery (groin) ruled out Sunday
items.desc: The Texans have ruled out RB David Montgomery with a groin injury.
items.impact: Montgomery will end the day with 11 rushing yards on five carries. Woody Marks will see the bulk of the carries out of the Houston backfield for the remainder of the game.

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: Jake Elliott puts five points on the board in Week 5 loss
items.desc: Jake Elliott hit his only field-goal attempt and both PATs in Sunday's 19-17 loss to the Jaguars.
items.impact: Elliott's only field goal in Sunday's game seemed like a game-winner when he hit it.  The veteran kicker connected from 48 yards to give the Eagles a 17-16 lead with only eight seconds remaining in the contest. It still wasn't enough to finish off the Jaguars. Elliott has yet to miss any kicks through five weeks, connecting on five field goals and 11 PATs to this point.

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: Dallas Goedert comes up with six catches in Week 5
items.desc: Dallas Goedert caught 6-of-9 targets for 38 yards in Sunday's 19-17 loss to the Jaguars.
items.impact: Playing for the first time since Week 2, Goedert led the Eagles in targets and receptions on Sunday. Top wide receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring) missed a second consecutive game, so Goedert's volume was at least somewhat attributable to that. Still, the veteran TE has long been a trusted target for QB Jalen Hurts. Goedert is coming off career bests with 60 receptions and 11 touchdowns last season.

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: Darius Cooper finds the end zone again in Week 5
items.desc: Darius Cooper brought down 2-of-3 targets for 71 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 19-17 loss to the Jaguars.
items.impact: With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) missing each of the last two games, Cooper has now hit paydirt three times over the last two weeks and four times this season. The second-year pro is certainly proving himself as a big-play option for QB Jalen Hurts, but Cooper is still limited in the volume of targets thrown his way.

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: Makai Lemon finishes with five receptions in Week 5
items.desc: Makai Lemon caught 5-of-7 targets for 43 yards in Sunday's 19-17 loss to the Jaguars.
items.impact: Lemon caught 10 passes over the first four weeks of the season. The first-round rookie set a new career high with five receptions in Sunday's game. With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) sidelined for the second straight game, the Eagles needed more out of their other wide receivers. Lemon helped out Sunday, but he's still yet to have a real breakout performance.

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: Dontayvion Wicks hauls in five passes Sunday
items.desc: Dontayvion Wicks secured 5-of-8 targets for 63 yards in Sunday's 19-17 loss to the Jaguars.
items.impact: With top wideout DeVonta Smith (hamstring) out for the second straight week, Wicks saw a season high in targets Sunday. He also tied a season high with five receptions and crossed the 60-yard mark for the third time in the first five weeks. Wicks is at least in the flex conversation for standard leagues right now.
